interface.name: deck_widget_manager_v1
interface.description: Global interface for Deck widget management. Widgets bind to this interface to obtain a deck_widget_surface_v1 for their wl_surface. The compositor identifies the connecting widget via SO_PEERCRED on the Wayland socket — there is no out-of-band identity handshake.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the widget manager. Does not affect existing widget surfaces.

request.name: get_widget_surface
request.description: Create a deck_widget_surface_v1 for the given wl_surface. The compositor identifies the widget from the peer credentials of the Wayland connection and emits initial configuration (configure, params, setting events, configure_done) against the new surface. The wl_surface must not already have a role.

entry.name: unknown_client
entry.summary: compositor has no initial config for this client

interface.name: deck_widget_manager_v2
interface.description:
Global interface for creating a widget surface identified by its configured widget instance key.
The global must be advertised at version 2 because get_widget_surface creates a surface at the manager resource version. Surface version 2 carries credential state.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the widget manager. Does not affect existing widget surfaces.

request.name: get_widget_surface
request.description: Create a deck_widget_surface_v1 for the given wl_surface and canonical configured-widget UUID. The wl_surface must not already have a role.

entry.name: invalid_key
entry.summary: widget instance key is not canonical

entry.name: unknown_widget
entry.summary: widget instance is not accepting connections

interface.name: deck_widget_surface_v1
interface.description:
Interface for a widget surface. On surface creation, the compositor emits initial configuration as a sequence of events, terminated by configure_done:
configure(width, height, viewport_shape, token) display_info(width, height, shape, dpi) params(json) timezone / night_mode / date_format / ... (setting events) configure_done
The widget must wait for configure_done before starting to render. After configure_done, the same setting events continue to flow whenever system settings change. Widget readiness is detected when the first buffer is committed.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the widget surface role. The wl_surface remains valid.

request.name: play_sound
request.description: Ask the compositor to play a system sound. The sound must be one of the names registered with the compositor's sound manager.

request.name: led_temporary

description.summary: run an LED effect for a finite duration

request.description:
The compositor will run the given effect for `duration_ms` milliseconds, then return to whatever LED state was active before the request. `period_ms` controls per-effect animation speed and is ignored for effects that have no notion of period (e.g. `solid`). A `period_ms` of 0 means "use the effect's default".
`request_id` is a widget-allocated identifier; the compositor replies with a `led_request_status` event whose `request_id` echoes this value as the request progresses (accepted, then eventually expired or superseded). The widget's namespace is scoped to its own surface — different widgets can reuse the same numeric value without collision. The value 0 is reserved for stop-all semantics on `stop_led` and must not be used here.

arg.name: request_id
arg.summary: widget-allocated request id, must be non-zero

arg.name: period_ms
arg.summary: animation period in milliseconds, 0 for default

arg.name: scope
arg.summary: led_scope.local for scene-scoped requests, led_scope.global for ambient signals

request.name: led_endless
request.description:
The compositor will run the given effect until a `led_temporary`, another `led_endless`, or `stop_led` request supersedes it. `period_ms` controls per-effect animation speed and is ignored for effects that have no notion of period. A `period_ms` of 0 means "use the effect's default".
See `led_temporary` for the semantics of `request_id` and the `led_request_status` reply.

arg.name: request_id
arg.summary: widget-allocated request id, must be non-zero

arg.name: period_ms
arg.summary: animation period in milliseconds, 0 for default

arg.name: scope
arg.summary: led_scope.local for scene-scoped requests, led_scope.global for ambient signals

request.name: stop_led
request.description: Cancel an LED request the widget previously made. If `request_id` is non-zero, only the matching request is cancelled; if zero, every LED request the widget owns is cancelled. `stop_led` is always accepted by the compositor and produces no `led_request_status` reply on its own — but cancelled requests receive a `superseded` status under their original ids.

arg.name: request_id
arg.summary: widget request id to cancel, 0 for all of this widget's

event.name: configure

description.summary: widget geometry, viewport shape, and instance identity

event.description: Delivered once on surface creation. Carries the widget's pixel dimensions, the shape of its viewport, and the opaque, stable per-instance token (usable to key per-instance resources such as an asset cache; stable across dormancy and restart). Follow-up `param_*` and setting events refine configuration; the batch is terminated by `configure_done`.

event.name: display_info
event.description: Delivered once on surface creation, after `configure` and before `configure_done`. Carries the active display's logical pixel size, shape, and DPI so widgets can adapt panel-wide rendering (e.g. corner masking on a round panel). DPI is the platform's real display density and is advisory during this development stage.

event.name: params
event.description:
The widget's per-instance params, exactly as stored in the scene configuration. A JSON-encoded object whose keys and value types match the widget's manifest. The compositor does not parse or validate this — the widget owns its manifest and is authoritative on what values are meaningful.
Emitted on surface creation as part of the initial configure batch, and re-emitted at runtime whenever the widget's params change (via an update that keeps the widget's geometry stable). An empty JSON object ("{}") is sent when no params are configured.

event.name: configure_done
event.description: Terminates the initial configure batch. After this event the widget has every piece of initial configuration the compositor intends to deliver and may start rendering. Subsequent setting events represent runtime changes.

event.name: timezone
event.description: Current timezone, IANA identifier (e.g. "Europe/Prague"). Sent on connect and whenever the timezone changes.

event.name: night_mode
event.description: Whether night mode is active. Sent on connect and on toggle.

event.name: next_alarm
event.description:
Soonest upcoming alarm derived host-side from the operator's alarm list. Sent on connect and whenever the next-to-fire entry changes (alarm add/edit/delete/fire/snooze, or timezone change).
`fire_at_utc_ms_hi` and `fire_at_utc_ms_lo` carry the high and low 32 bits of a signed 64-bit milliseconds-since-UNIX-epoch timestamp, matching the hi/lo split pattern from wp_presentation_feedback. Both args are zero when `present` is `absent`.

arg.name: fire_at_utc_ms_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the signed 64-bit ms timestamp

arg.name: fire_at_utc_ms_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the signed 64-bit ms timestamp

arg.name: name

event.name: lifecycle
event.description:
Emitted whenever the widget's lifecycle state changes. The initial emission immediately after the configure_done batch is always one of the idle states: 'dormant', 'prepared', or 'visible'. The transitional states 'entering' and 'leaving' only appear during an active scene transition, never as a first event.
Within a scene change the compositor emits a release batch (transitions into 'dormant') and flushes it, then emits the acquire batch (all other transitions) and flushes again. This ordering lets a shared render-target pool be reclaimed before the next acquire and is the only ordering guarantee the compositor makes between batches.
Permitted transitions (the compositor never emits anything else): dormant -> prepared | visible | entering prepared -> dormant | visible | entering visible -> dormant | prepared | leaving entering -> visible | prepared | dormant leaving -> dormant | prepared | visible
Widgets that do not bind this event silently ignore it; old widgets keep working unchanged.

event.name: shutdown
event.description: Sent when the widget should shut down gracefully. Widget should clean up and exit.

event.name: transition_incoming

description.summary: automatic scene transition will show this widget soon

event.description: Emitted during automatic scene cycling pre-transition for widgets in the incoming scene. This is a one-shot warm-up instruction: hosts should render one fresh frame if the widget is currently renderable, but must not enable animation frame callbacks for non-visible lifecycle states. Manual scene drags do not emit this event; they are represented only by lifecycle changes.

event.name: led_request_status

description.summary: status update for an LED request

event.description:
Lifecycle update for a previous `led_temporary` or `led_endless` request. `request_id` echoes the value the widget supplied.
Status semantics: - accepted: the request entered the queue (or was activated immediately). - rejected: the compositor refused the request without running it. Reserved for a future permissions layer; current implementations only emit accepted/superseded/expired. - superseded: an endless was displaced from its tier — by `stop_led`, by another endless landing on the same tier (the previous holder loses the slot and will not come back), or by the widget disconnecting. - expired: a `led_temporary`'s duration ran out on its logical-time schedule. Fires whether or not the strip was showing the effect at the moment.
`led_endless` requests never receive `expired`; they end with `superseded` once displaced or cancelled.

event.name: credentials

description.summary: which credential slots are bound, and to what

event.description:
The widget's credential slots that currently resolve to a saved account, as a JSON-encoded object keyed by manifest slot name: {"SLOT": {"type": "CREDENTIAL-TYPE-ID", "account": "OPERATOR-CHOSEN-NAME"}}. A slot absent from the object is unbound, whether the operator never bound it or bound it to an account that no longer exists.
Carries no secret material and is safe to log. This is the whole of what a widget may learn about its credentials; the values themselves arrive on credential_secrets and stop at the widget process.
Emitted on surface creation as part of the initial configure batch, and re-emitted whenever the resolution changes. An empty JSON object ("{}") is sent when nothing is bound.
A version-1 peer never receives this event, and reads every slot as unbound.

event.name: credential_secrets

description.summary: secret field values for the bound slots

event.description:
The secret field values behind each bound slot, as a JSON-encoded object keyed by manifest slot name: {"SLOT": {"fields": {"FIELD": "VALUE"}, "allow_hosts": ["HOST", …]}}. Slot keys match the credentials event exactly. allow_hosts is the account's own egress pin in the catalog's pin grammar; absent or empty, the slot's credential type decides.
This event carries live secrets and must never be forwarded to guest WASM, written to a log, or persisted. The widget process is trusted to hold it and to substitute the values into outbound requests on the widget's behalf; the widget itself never sees them.
Emitted alongside credentials, on the same occasions.

enum.name: lifecycle_state
enum.description: Tracks whether the widget is on-screen, neighbouring an on-screen widget, transitioning in or out under a scene-cycle drag, or completely off-screen. The host runtime uses this to acquire and release render-target buffers and to gate animation ticking.

enum.name: viewport_shape
enum.description: Shape of the region the widget renders into. Kept separate from `display_shape` so viewport shapes can evolve independently of panel shapes in future versions of the protocol. Today both enums declare the same two values.

enum.name: display_shape
enum.description: Shape of the visible display area. Advisory layout metadata; the widget coordinate space stays rectangular regardless of shape.

entry.name: local
entry.summary: scene-scoped; hidden while the widget's scene is not active

entry.name: global
entry.summary: system-wide; runs when no local effect is active on the strip

entry.name: accepted
entry.summary: request entered the queue or became active

entry.name: superseded
entry.summary: endless was displaced from its tier and will not come back

entry.name: expired
entry.summary: led_temporary's duration ran out on its logical-time schedule
